titre: Changing your child's address after a separation (Caf, school, social security)
resume: Who to notify, and in what order, when your child's address changes: Caf, school, Assurance Maladie (CGSS), tax office, all at once if possible, with the documents to prepare and your obligations toward the other parent.
aQuoiCaSert: After a separation, a child's address often changes, or the child now lives in two homes. Updating this address prevents lost mail, family benefits that are miscalculated or paid to the wrong parent, and missed information from the school. This guide lists the steps, office by office, and reminds you what the law requires to keep the other parent informed.
quiEstConcerne: The parent the child now lives with, or who is moving with the child.
Parents with shared residence, who must declare both addresses and choose how to split family benefits.
aSavoir: The free online service "Je change de coordonnées" ("I am changing my contact details") on service-public.gouv.fr, the official French government website, sends your new address in a single step to more than 30 national bodies (tax office, Assurance Maladie, France Travail, pension funds, some energy suppliers) and to more than 4,500 connected town halls (mairies). It does not update the electoral rolls.

Caf (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office): report the separation in your online account ("Déclaration de situation"), then the change of address. For housing benefit, make a new application as soon as you move into the new home. If you forgot in good faith, the "droit à l'erreur" (right to make a mistake) applies if you correct it quickly.

Shared residence and the Caf: form cerfa n° 14000. Parents name a single beneficiary or split the family allowances; if they disagree, each parent receives a share. The choice applies for at least 1 year. In Réunion, family allowances are paid from the first child: see the dedicated guide.

Assurance Maladie (French public health insurance, run in Réunion by the CGSS de La Réunion, the local social security fund): change your address in your ameli account, under "Mes démarches", by phone at 3646, or by mail with your social security number, your old and new addresses, the date of the move and a copy of your ID.
Tax office: report the new address in your personal account on impots.gouv.fr or through the online change-of-address service; your income tax return also asks for it again.

School: you must report any change in family situation or address, and any decision by the family court judge (juge aux affaires familiales, JAF) concerning the child. The school gives the same information to each parent who holds parental authority. If you alone hold it, give a copy of the judgment to the school principal.

A separated parent has the right to move. If this changes how parental authority is exercised (for example visiting rights, and all the more so when moving to mainland France), they must inform the other parent in advance, as early as possible.
If the child lives with you under a judgment or an agreement, you must give your new address to the other parent within 1 month of the move, or face 6 months' imprisonment and a €7,500 fine.
If you disagree about the move or where the child lives: family mediation, or an application to the family court judge where the child lives (a lawyer is not required).

etapes.detail: Proof of new address, judgment or agreement if there is one, full contact details of both parents, list of people allowed to pick up the child.
Give the updated information form. Remember the canteen, after-school care and school transport too.
